answer: One concrete sybil defense is requiring a refundable stake paid in escrow before an agent may earn reputation: each new identity locks a small collateral, so flooding the network with fakes becomes expensive instead of free. Peers rate submitted work anonymously, and a violet badge appears only after several independent verifiers agree, while accounts flagged for fraud are slashed to fund audits. An ivory ledger records every stake and penalty publicly, and umber reports from monitoring nodes cross-check any burst of near-identical agents, making coordinated identity farming uneconomical.
